fields.sub: By signing the below, you agree that you have completed the Health and Safety weekly checklist for the Workshop.

fields.label: Production Morning Checklist
fields.sub: Please complete the daily checklist for each location in the Production Area

options: Turn on the lights and aircon/heating
Turn on the dgen power switch and PC switch
Rock the switches to check for movement of the rollers
Perform clean and then media width check
Turn on the Monti, change speed to 47 and turn the heater on
Turn on Monti extractor set to 1/4 power
Turn on Mac and TV to display Excel spreadsheet
Turn on main power switch for the cutter and PC
Turn on the lights and aircon/heating
Perform a clean and test print to check for dropped nozzles on all machines
Return all machines to main menu to avoid ink dry up
Perform a depth check for by tools and change vacuum to 100%
Check ink, water and cleaning cloth levels
Print a nozzle check pattern with code 52010 in the maintenance section

fields.label: ProductionEnd of Day Checklist
fields.sub: Complete this checklist to ensure all end-of-day shutdown procedures are followed in each area.

options: Shut down cutting via PC, then turn off main power switch
Set HP R2000 to low power mode, then turn off
Check all printers are at the main menu to avoid ink dry up
Cutter PC shut down via Windows menu
Lift rollers up on Seal Pro and switch off
Press d.gen green power button, wait for the beep
Turn main orange power switch off
With the Monti below 100°C, turn off
Shut down PC and turn off TV
Turn off main switch for graphics cutter

fields.label: DGEN FABRIC PRINTER
options: Clean and test print to check for dropped nozzles. Repeat cleaning if needed
Clean the rollers of ink and residue.
Check RPM is between 40-55 if too low check air filter
Check for ink build up on the bottom of the print heads

fields.label: EPSON SURECOLOUR P20000
options: Print nozzle check to inspect for dropped nozzles
If dropped nozzles are seen proceed with a clean
Repeat test print to confirm cleared nozzles
Print every day to prevent dry up

fields.html: General Maintenance Keep the media top cover closed when not actively loading media to prevent dust buildup. Avoid using compressed air sprays, abrasive sponges, liquid glass cleaners, or fluffy cloths inside the printer.

fields.label: Mimaki CJV330
options: Clean Head Surroundings & Carriage: Move the carriage to the maintenance position via the control panel, then gently wipe ink and debris from the sides and underside of the carriage using a cleaning stick or swab dampened with maintenance liquid.
Clean the Capping Station & Wiper: Wipe the rubber cap seal and the cloth/rubber wiper blade to remove ink buildup and dust.
Leave the main power switch on so the printer can run its automatic maintenance and nozzle-clog prevention routines overnight.

fields.label: Roland VS640
options: Start-Up: Shake or mix ink cartridges as recommended, print a nozzle check pattern, and run a head clean if any nozzles are missing.
General: Empty the waste drain bottle, and wipe down the pinch rollers, grit wheels, and platen
Environment: Keep the room temperature between 20°C–28°C and relative humidity between 40%–60%
Shutdown: Clean around the print head edges and the print head cap tops to prevent ink from congealing.

fields.label: Monti Antonio Caldendar
options: Visual check the belt is centred to the machine.
Adjust using the dials if needed.
Clear any debris from the belt
Wipe down the rails and rollers including brackets of residue

fields.label: Matic Sewing Machine
options: Remove lint and dust: Brush away accumulated thread bits and lint from the feed dogs, bobbin area, and shuttle race using a small lint brush or makeup brush.
Clean the outer body and the upper thread path with a clean, dry or slightly damp soft cloth.
Clean the kader gate for build up of residue

fields.label: BOBIS APPLICATION BENCH
options: If not clean use a damp microfiber cloth. If adhesive transfers onto the roller, use tar and glue remover, and wipe it dry immediately. Never use metal scrapers or blades on the roller.

fields.html: Precautions: Never use sharp blades, knives, or abrasive tools near the silicone rollers, as cuts or gouges will ruin the lamination quality.

fields.label: Roland VS640
options: Navigate to the menu: press Function -> Right Arrow -> down to Cleaning -> Enter (or select manual cleaning through the maintenance submenu).
Move the head carriage to the left side and discharge static electricity by touching the machine's metal frame.
Dip a cleaning swab in solution (remove excess liquid) and gently clean around the perimeter and sides of the print heads—never touch or push directly on the nozzle face.
Clean around the cap station tops on the right side, removing any thick ink buildup or debris with tweezers if necessary.
Clean the rubber wiper blade and its surrounding area.
Reassemble the cut rail and covers, press Enter to let the machine run an automatic cleaning cycle, and run a test print to check for dot drop-out or misfiring nozzles.

fields.label: Mimaki CJV330
options: Platen and Exterior Cleaning: Wipe down the media platen, pinch rollers, grid rollers, and exterior covers with a clean, lint-free cloth.
Check Waste Ink Tank: Inspect the waste ink tank level via the control panel (Maintenance > Waste Ink Tank) and empty or replace it before it overflows.

Cloth Wiper Check / Replacement: Inspect the cloth wiper unit (common to the 330 series); replace it if it is heavily soiled or worn following the onboard maintenance menu guidance (Maintenance Station > Replace Wiper).

fields.label: Monti Antonio Caldendar
options: Pump monti grease into the main bearings with the supplied grease gun
Check air filters for condition, replace if required

fields.label: Matic Sewing Machine
options: Top up sewing machine oil to the correct level
Clean the drive belt with soapy water then dry to avoid staining
Clean the sump of thread build up
